title: Design feedback & critique

body.text: Claude is a bias-free critique partner:
send the work and ask for feedback against criteria: hierarchy, contrast, consistency, usability
— you get a fresh perspective before shipping, especially when you've stared at your own work until it all looks normal.

example: "Critique this poster directly: where does the eye go first, is the main message prominent enough, is anything competing for attention"

title: Give and take feedback like a pro

body.text: The AI also helps on the communication side:
turn a client's vague feedback ('it doesn't wow me') into an actionable fix list
and help you write up your design rationale so the client understands the reasoning behind it.

example: "The client said 'it looks too plain' — interpret that into 5 possibilities, with questions to ask back to find the real meaning"

question: When asking the AI for a design critique, what should you specify?

options.text: Clear criteria, like hierarchy, contrast, usability

question: The client says 'it doesn't wow me' — what can the AI help with?

options.text: Interpret the possibilities and ask questions to find the real meaning
Make it 'wow' on its own without asking

question: Why is an AI critique useful before shipping?

options.text: You get a fresh perspective when your eyes have gotten used to your own work
No human review is ever needed again

question: What should giving design feedback like a pro be like?

options.text: Just say you don't like it
Specific, tied to the goal, and proposing fixes

question: How do you use Claude to help critique design work?

options.text: Ask for a perspective based on UX principles and the target audience
